questions: Tell me about yourself and what drew you into software engineering.
Why are you interested in this role and our company?
Walk me through a project you are proud of and what your part in it was.
Tell me about a time you tracked down a particularly difficult bug and how you found the cause.
Describe a time you disagreed with a teammate about a technical decision and how it was resolved.
How do you approach writing code that is easy to test and maintain?
What do you look for when you review a colleague's pull request?
Tell me about a time you had to learn a new language or framework quickly to deliver something.
Describe a time you missed or nearly missed a deadline and what you did about it.
How would you explain a hash table and how it handles collisions to a new teammate?
Tell me about a time you received critical feedback on your code and what you did with it.
Suppose a production release is failing and the team is stressed; what do you do in the first hour?
good_answer_tips: Walk through your reasoning out loud, including trade-offs, rather than jumping to an answer.
Use a concrete project with your specific contribution and a measurable outcome.
Show ownership of mistakes and what you changed afterward.
Mention testing, code review, and communication with non-engineers.
red_flags: Blaming teammates or past employers for problems.
Vague answers with no specific project or result.
Claiming never to have made a mistake or received hard feedback.

questions: Tell me a little about yourself and why you want to work in customer service.
How would you define great customer service?
Tell me about a time you turned an angry customer into a satisfied one.
What do you do first when a customer is yelling at you over the phone?
Do you believe the customer is always right, and why or why not?
How do you handle a customer asking for something that is against company policy?
What would you do if you did not know the answer to a customer's question?
Tell me about a time you went above and beyond for a customer.
How do you stay calm and organized when the queue is long and several customers are waiting?
Which customer support or CRM tools have you used, and how do you pick up new software?
Tell me about a time you made a mistake with a customer and how you fixed it.
How would you contact a customer about a problem when you do not yet have all the answers?
good_answer_tips: Name steps: listen, empathize, apologize where fair, solve, follow up.
Give a real example with the customer outcome.
Show respect for policy while looking for the best allowed option.
Show patience and a calm tone under pressure.
red_flags: Arguing with or blaming the customer.
Saying you would simply pass the customer along without follow-through.
Having no example of a difficult interaction.

questions: Tell me about yourself and why you want to work in retail.
Why do you want to work at our store specifically?
Tell me about your previous retail or customer-facing experience.
How would you greet and help a customer who walks in and seems unsure what they want?
How do you recommend extra products without sounding pushy?
Describe a time you dealt with an upset customer, such as at a return counter.
What would you do if several customers needed help at the same moment?
What would you do if a customer asked about a product you knew nothing about?
What experience do you have with cash registers and handling money accurately?
How would you react if you saw a coworker or customer stealing?
Tell me about a time you worked with a team to hit a goal, like a sale or inventory push.
How do you stay on your feet and positive during a long, busy shift?
good_answer_tips: Show warmth and initiative, like greeting and approaching customers.
Mention accuracy with cash, returns, and store policy.
Give examples of teamwork and flexibility with schedules.
Explain helping customers find value rather than pushing sales.
red_flags: Ignoring the customer or being dismissive about the work.
Handling theft confrontationally instead of following policy and alerting a manager.
Complaining about past managers or customers.

questions: Tell me about your experience as a server and what you enjoy about it.
Why do you want to work at our restaurant?
How do you keep track of several tables during a busy rush?
Tell me about a time a guest was unhappy with their food or service and how you handled it.
How do you handle a guest who tells you they have a food allergy?
What would you do if you noticed a coworker was falling behind while you were also busy?
How would you describe and recommend menu items to a guest who cannot decide?
What experience do you have with point-of-sale systems?
Tell me about a time you made an order mistake and what you did.
How do you stay upbeat and efficient on a long, hectic shift?
What would you do if the kitchen ran out of a popular dish after a guest ordered it?
Tell me about a time you worked well with kitchen staff or teammates to fix a problem.
good_answer_tips: Show how you prioritize tables and communicate with kitchen and team.
Treat allergies seriously: confirm with the kitchen and manager.
Describe repairing a bad experience with a calm, quick fix.
Mention teamwork, reliability, and being on time.
red_flags: Guessing about allergens or minimizing allergy safety.
Blaming kitchen or guests for problems.
Unwillingness to help teammates or work weekends and busy shifts.

questions: Tell me about yourself and why you chose nursing.
Why do you want to work on this unit at our hospital?
Describe a time a patient's condition began to deteriorate and what you did.
A patient on your unit suddenly becomes unresponsive; what are your first steps?
How do you prioritize care when you have several patients who all need you at once?
Tell me about a time you disagreed with a physician or colleague about patient care.
How do you support a laboring patient and her family when labor is long or not going as planned?
How would you respond if a patient in labor or postpartum showed signs of heavy bleeding?
How would you handle a patient who refuses a recommended treatment?
Tell me about a time you made or nearly made a medication error and what happened afterward.
Describe a time you dealt with a difficult or upset patient or family member.
How do you take care of yourself and manage stress after emotionally hard shifts?
good_answer_tips: Use clear clinical steps such as assess, escalate, and communicate with SBAR.
Put patient safety and advocacy first in every example.
Give specific outcomes and what you learned.
Show teamwork and respectful communication with providers.
red_flags: Hiding or downplaying errors instead of reporting them.
Acting alone without escalating in an emergency.
Dismissing patient or family concerns.

questions: What inspired you to become a speech-language pathologist?
Why are you interested in working in this school or clinic setting?
How do you decide whether a child is eligible for speech and language services?
How do you plan therapy sessions that keep young children engaged?
Tell me about a child who was not making progress and what you changed.
How do you collect data and monitor progress toward goals?
How do you write and run an IEP meeting so that parents feel included?
How do you work with classroom teachers to carry therapy goals into the classroom?
How do you manage a large caseload and paperwork deadlines?
Tell me about a time you disagreed with a parent or colleague about a child's services.
How would you support a family who is frustrated or in denial about their child's diagnosis?
How do you work with students from culturally and linguistically diverse backgrounds?
good_answer_tips: Cite evidence-based methods and data-driven decisions.
Describe family and teacher collaboration with concrete examples.
Show cultural sensitivity and ethical practice.
Explain how you adjust therapy when progress stalls.
red_flags: No mention of data or progress monitoring.
Dismissive attitude toward parents or teachers.
A one-size-fits-all approach to therapy.

questions: Tell me about yourself and what made you decide to become a teacher.
How would you describe your teaching philosophy?
How do you set up and manage your classroom at the start of the year?
Tell me about a time a student was disruptive and how you handled it.
How do you differentiate instruction for students at different levels?
How do you support students with IEPs or 504 plans?
How do you motivate a student who seems disengaged?
How do you communicate with parents, especially when there is a concern?
Describe a lesson that went badly and what you changed afterward.
How do you use technology and assessment data to improve your teaching?
Tell me about a time you collaborated with colleagues to help a student succeed.
How would you respond if a parent strongly disagreed with a grade you gave?
good_answer_tips: Give concrete classroom examples with student outcomes.
Show proactive classroom management built on relationships and clear routines.
Explain how you use assessment data to adjust instruction.
Show respectful, regular communication with families.
red_flags: Blaming students or parents for problems.
Relying only on punishment for classroom management.
Having no plan for students who need extra support.
